questions.q: According to Section 20 of RA 9266, what two specific items must a Registered and Licensed Architect sign and seal on every page of their architectural plans and documents?
o: Registration Number and Professional Tax Receipt (PTR) number
Architectural Firm Name and SEC Registration
IAPOA Membership number and Tax Identification Number (TIN)
questions.n: These two identifiers verify the architect's current legal standing and tax compliance for the specific locality and year.

questions.q: Under Section 31 of RA 9266, who is specifically defined as the 'Architect-of-Record'?
o: The architect who is directly and professionally responsible for the total design and signs the documents
The architect who manages the construction site on a daily basis
The architect who acts as a consultant for specialized systems
The government architect who reviews the building permit
questions.n: The Architect-of-Record (AoR) carries the legal and professional liability for the entire design phase.

questions.q: Which section of RA 9266 specifies the penal provisions, including fines ranging from Php 100,000 to Php 5,000,000, for violators of the Act?
questions.n: Section 29 details the fines and imprisonment terms for unauthorized practice and other violations of the Architecture Act.

questions.q: According to Section 25, how many days does the Board have to report the examination ratings to the Commission after the examination is held?
questions.n: The Board must report ratings within 30 days unless an extension is granted for technical reasons.

questions.q: Under Section 37, what is the specific mandate regarding the 'IAPOA'?
o: That all architects must join at least three different professional clubs
That IAPOA is responsible for conducting the board exams
That there shall be only one integrated and accredited professional organization of architects
That IAPOA membership is optional for government architects
questions.n: The law mandates a single, unified organization (currently UAP) to ensure professional standards and cohesion.

questions.q: In SPP Doc 301, what is the 'Retention' percentage usually held from the contractor's progress billings to ensure the completion of the project?
questions.n: The 10% retention acts as a security for the Owner against potential defects or uncompleted work.

questions.q: How many days before the desired payment date must the contractor submit the Request for Payment to the architect?
questions.n: Contractors must submit their request 15 days in advance to allow for inspection and administrative processing.

questions.q: Within how many days must the architect issue the Certificate of Payment after receiving the contractor's request?
questions.n: The architect has one week to verify the work and issue the certification for the owner to pay.

questions.q: What is the 'Liability Period' for the contractor regarding structural defects or collapse, as per the Civil Code often referenced in Doc 301?
questions.n: Both the architect and the contractor are liable for 15 years if a building collapses due to defects in plans or construction.

questions.q: If the owner terminates the contract for 'Convenience,' what is the minimum notice period required to be given to the contractor?
questions.n: A 15-day written notice allows for an orderly shutdown and settlement of costs.

questions.q: Which service under SPP Doc 203 involves the design of the built environment's physical settings, including walkways, gardens, and water features?
questions.n: This specialized service focuses on the integration of nature and hardscape elements surrounding the building.

questions.q: What specialized service under Doc 203 focuses on the internal space of a building, including furniture, finishes, and lighting?
questions.n: Interior Design deals with the human-scale experience, aesthetics, and functionality inside the building shell.

questions.q: Which specialized service involves the design of a building’s lighting, acoustics, and communication systems?
questions.n: While part of MEP, this service focuses on the atmospheric and technical lighting quality as a specialized architectural skill.

questions.q: What is the definition of 'Physical Planning' under Doc 203?
o: Calculating the thermal mass of a wall
The design of land areas for various uses, such as subdivisions and estates
Designing the structural frame of a building
questions.n: Physical planning involves site-wide layouts for large-scale developments and zoning logic.

questions.q: Which service involves the detailed study of a building’s environmental impact and its energy efficiency to achieve high performance?
questions.n: Also known as Green Building Design, this service aims for ratings like LEED or BERDE.

questions.q: What is the 'Space Planning' service as defined in SPP Doc 201 (Pre-Design Services)?
o: Determining size and configuration of spaces based on client needs
Choosing the paint colors for a room
questions.n: In pre-design, space planning translates the program into a physical spatial arrangement.

questions.q: Which service involves evaluating the economic and technical viability of a proposed project?
questions.n: A feasibility study tells the owner if the project is worth doing before any money is spent on full design.

questions.q: What is the primary goal of the 'Site Selection and Analysis' service in Doc 201?
o: Evaluating potential sites based on location and accessibility
questions.n: The architect analyzes topography, utilities, and traffic to determine the best location for the project.
